newsitem.title: UK: UK's shares seen resuming advance next week.
newsitem.headline: UK's shares seen resuming advance next week.

text.p: The leading UK blue chip index is poised to revisit its all-time peak next week, led by Wall Street, as the latest figures on U.S. wholesale inflation dispelled fears of a near-term rate hike, dealers and strategists said.
With UK results season winding down, the UK equity market will turn its attention to the U.S. where investors will continue to sniff around for signs of inflation, they said.
Wednesday's consumer price index data could provide more clues ahead of the Federal Reserve's March 25 policy meeting.
"There isn't one domestic figure that's setting the tone in the UK market. We're being pushed around by Wall Street," said Nick Knight, global equity strategist with Nomura.
"And one has learned never to say never when it comes to what Wall Street will do next," he added.
Yet dealers and strategists said the UK market's underlying tone remains strong, and the FTSE 100's rebound over the 4,400 market bodes well for the near term.
"There are still a lot of shorts out there. I think we'll see the market squeeze higher," said one senior dealer.

Added Credit Lyonnais Laing strategist Cory Miller, "Valuations in the UK are looking a little bit stretched. But the fact is that the market still has a strong undertone. Institutions are still looking to get back into the market."
But it will be an uphill struggle for UK blue chips on Monday when 11 big FTSE 100 stocks go ex-dividend, slicing 22.09 points off the FTSE 100 share index.
There are only a handful of blue chips set to release annual results. They include Pearson Plc, Wolseley Plc, Kingfisher Plc and Guinness Plc.
More than a dozen second-tier companies are due to report their earnings.

UK economic data due next week include UK February public sector borrowing requirement, February retail sales and unemployment data, retail prices, money supply for February and the CBI monthly survey.
In the U.S., February housing starts and real earnings for February are due, but the focus will be on the consumer price index for February, dealers said.
